where: the whole edit sheet — every field between the amber banner and the sticky Cancel / Save changes footer; same construction on sync-blocked
finding: Marcus opens Edit profile on a record whose last edit went out 14 seconds ago and finds a form he cannot type in. Not the managed fields — every field. Notes and Status are dead too, and the brief's own must-not-change list says Notes and roster status are Tally's own, are not in the queue and are never blocked by it. sync-blocked makes the contradiction visible on one screen: its amber banner says in so many words "Notes are Tally's own and can be typed now", and the Notes box a scroll below it is greyed out. Nothing on the glass separates the fields that belong to Planning Center from the two that belong to Tally, so a leader learns the rule by poking at boxes.
evidence: In the open dialog of both sync-editor--phone.html and sync-blocked--phone.html all eight controls carry `disabled` — first name, last name, nickname, grade select, birthday, allergies, notes textarea, status select — and every hint underneath reads either "Saved in Planning Center" or the ordinary field help ("Visible to the core team…" under the dead Notes box). The closed variant in the same file uses a distinct "Managed in Planning Center" hint; the rendered one does not. Frames: sync-blocked--phone-full at the Notes block, sync-editor--phone-full at the same place.
direction: The lock has to stop at the Planning Center boundary. Managed fields dim with a hint that names the reason; Notes and Status keep full contrast and a live Save path, because they land instantly and always have.

where: the sheet as a whole, and the sticky footer at the bottom of the 844px screen
finding: The refinement exists to stop a leader waiting on Planning Center, and this frame moves the wait from the Save button onto the entire form. Marcus came to fix a surname in eight seconds; the surname box is dead, the banner tells him "These boxes unlock as soon as it lands", and on busy church wifi that is the same thirty-to-forty-five seconds the brief says nobody can fix — except now he has to hold the screen awake to spend it. The only live control on the screen is Save changes, which has nothing to save. It is also the brightest and lowest thing on the page, so it is exactly what a thumb goes to, and tapping it promises nothing. And the lock forbids a case the brief names outright: "Dana saves, spots her own typo, saves again three seconds later… the second should replace it." On this screen she cannot.
evidence: sync-editor--phone-fold: banner "Your last change is still saving / Last name and grade went to Planning Center 14 seconds ago. These boxes unlock as soon as it lands, so two edits cannot cross." All fields disabled (opacity-50); the footer Cancel and Save changes are min-h-14 = 56 CSS px, Save at flex-[2] taking roughly two-thirds of the 390px width, and neither carries `disabled`. The profile that leads here (sync-profile--phone-fold) shows Edit profile as a live 44px brand button 28px under Undo, with no hint that the form behind it is frozen — so the trip is two taps and a scroll before he learns.
direction: Do not lock the leader who owns the queued job out of their own record: let a second save supersede an unclaimed first, which is what the brief asks for anyway. Keep a lock — or better, a warning that names who and when — for the other-leader collision in J5, and say on the profile button, before the sheet opens, if the record is not currently editable.

where: the roster rows, top of the list — Sofia Okonkwo is the fourth and last full row above the fold
finding: Nothing on a row says an edit landed. Sofia's row is blank, and a row whose surname correction confirmed upstream ten seconds ago would be blank in exactly the same way as a row nobody has ever touched. J2 is Dana with nine edits in four minutes needing to tell, at a glance down the list, which are done — the list can only say which are not done. On a phone that is expensive: only four rows of forty-five fit above the fold, so checking she is finished means scrolling the whole list and confirming an absence on each screen. `differs` — the state the brief flags as the one most likely to be dropped as a nicety — has no mark at all, so a value the church office changed underneath her is indistinguishable from a clean row.
evidence: sync-students--phone-fold: the list starts at 513 CSS px down an 844px screen (title block, three stacked action buttons, search, two selects and two rows of filter chips come first) and the tab bar starts at 776, leaving 263 CSS px of list; rows are 128 device / 64 CSS px, so four fit. Across all 45 rows the full frame carries exactly four state words — Saving, Waiting, Queued, Needs you — and no green, no landed, no differs.
direction: A short-lived positive mark in `present` green for landed, and its own word for differs, both stating only that a job existed and how it ended — no edited value on the row, so the minors rule holds.

where: the state chips on rows 1, 2 and 11 — Ava Chen "Saving", Marcus Delacroix-Oyelaran "Waiting", Amara Whitfield "Queued"
finding: The three in-flight states are encoded so that a glance cannot sort them, and one of them is encoded as the wrong kind of thing. `sending` and `waiting` are the same amber, the same ◷ glyph, the same size and the same weight; only the word differs, at 11 CSS px, in a dim corridor. That is the pair the brief most needs kept apart — `waiting` must not read as stuck, and a leader who cannot tell a backed-off job from a live one starts retrying things that were fine. `queued` is worse: it is rendered in the same grey chip as "No contact" on the row directly below, so the one thing on Amara's row that will be different in a minute looks like a permanent property of the child.
evidence: sync-students--phone-fold, rows at device y1026–1279: both chips are bg-warn-500/15 / text-warn-400 with the same ◷ glyph, 42 device px = 21 CSS tall, text-[11px] font-semibold — the smallest information-carrying type on the screen carrying the fastest-changing fact. Amara's "Queued" chip (device y2300–2335 in the full frame) is bg-ink-800 / text-ink-300, byte-identical styling to the "No contact" chip 8 CSS px away.
direction: Let the glyph, not the word, carry the difference between sending and waiting, and lift state text off 11px. Put queued in the same in-flight family as the other two rather than in attribute-grey, so the row reads "something is happening here" before it is read at all.

where: the "Queued" chip on Amara Whitfield's row, second chip line, roughly two-thirds down the full list
finding: That chip is not a label, it is a button, and what it fires is a create in the church's permanent people database — the operation the brief says this codebase is most careful about duplicating. It measures 60 × 20 CSS px, under half the 44px floor in its smallest dimension, and it sits inside a row whose entire area is a link to the profile, 8 CSS px from two other grey chips of identical size that do different things. On a phone there is no hover to reveal which of the three is which. An 8px miss either opens a page or writes a child upstream, and nothing about the chip's appearance says which side of that line it is on.
evidence: sync-students--phone-full, device y2300–2335, x168–287 = 60 × 20 CSS px. Markup: <button type="button" title="Waiting to be created in Planning Center" aria-label="Amara Whitfield is not in Planning Center yet — push them now"> with the same bg-ink-800/ring-ink-700 chip class as the informational "No contact" button beside it; the row's <a class="absolute inset-0"> sits underneath and the chips win on z-index. The row is 64 CSS px tall, the chips are 20.
direction: On touch, a row state is a label and nothing more. "Push them now" belongs on the profile, where a 44px target and a sentence explaining what it writes both fit; the row only needs to say the link is queued.

where: "Fix and send again" and "Discard the edit", stacked inside the red banner at the top of the record
finding: Priya lands on a week-old refusal and the two moves are 7 CSS px apart. One reopens Marcus's correction; the other throws it away. They are the same height, the same radius, the same font, one under the other, and there is no dialog behind the destructive one. Standing up, one-handed, the boundary between them is thinner than the error of a thumb. J4 also asks for exactly one obvious next move, and this gives two of near-equal weight, so the frame reads as a choice when it should read as an instruction with an escape hatch.
evidence: sync-failed--phone-fold, measured on the pixels: Fix and send again occupies device y728–815 (88 = 44 CSS px tall), Discard the edit y830–921 (46 CSS px), gap y816–829 = 14 device = 7 CSS px. They are one flex-wrap gap-2 row that wraps at 390px, so the 8px meant as a horizontal gutter became the vertical separation between a retry and a delete.
direction: One full-width primary on phone; demote discard to low-emphasis text with at least a target's height of space above it, or move it inside the editor where the leader is already looking at what would be lost.

where: the amber "Saving to Planning Center" strip, and the absence of any offline variant of it across all five frames
finding: The brief calls Marcus in a basement corridor the ordinary case and asks for the tenth state hiding inside queued to get its own words: nothing has left this phone yet. No phone frame in this round says that, and the one frame that comes closest says the opposite — "It carries on without this page — you can close the tab." He has no tab. He has a lock button and one bar of signal, and the strip has just promised him, in the exact moment the promise is least likely to be true, that the edit is already somebody else's problem. He locks the phone believing the surname is fixed. The same strip also collapses two states in three lines: the heading says sending, the body says "queued by you", and the only action offered is Undo, which is honest in one of those readings and a lie in the other.
evidence: sync-profile--phone-fold, banner at device y432–755: title "Saving to Planning Center", body "Last name and grade, queued by you 14 seconds ago. It carries on without this page — you can close the tab.", one 44 CSS px brand button "Undo this edit". No frame in sync-r00 shows an offline or not-yet-left-the-device presentation, and no row chip covers it either.
direction: An offline variant of the same amber strip, phrased about the device rather than the tab, with a matching row chip; and pick one word for the state the strip is actually in, so that whether Undo can still work is readable from the heading rather than inferred from the button's presence.

where: the in-flight strip on sync-profile, and the states it does not have a variant for
finding: Three things the brief names have no frame at any width, and all three land on the phone persona. `stalled`: Marcus locks his phone and the job runs past two minutes — the strip would still read "Saving to Planning Center… 14 seconds ago" in the same amber and the same tone, and the brief is explicit that stalled must not read as failed but must read as something. `orphaned`: a queued edit against a record deleted upstream has no presentation, though the profile already carries the re-create move the brief points at. And the two-leader collision in J5 — Dana's edit in flight while Marcus opens the record in the corridor — has no frame; the strip only knows how to say "queued by you". The pattern for it already exists on sync-failed, which names Marcus Webb and last Tuesday.
evidence: Across all five phone frames the in-flight vocabulary is: Saving to Planning Center (profile), Your last change is still saving (editor), Amara is still being created (blocked), Planning Center refused this edit (failed), and the four row chips Saving / Waiting / Queued / Needs you. Nothing for stalled, orphaned, or an edit queued by somebody other than the reader.
direction: Reuse the sync-failed sentence shape — a person and a time — for the other-leader case, and give the strip a two-minute variant that changes tone without changing colour to danger.
